newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Fiji president visits Taiwan, risks China's ire.
newsitem.headline: Fiji president visits Taiwan, risks China's ire.

text.p: Fiji President Kamisese Mara arrived in Taiwan on Thursday for a six-day official visit that risks angering China -- Fiji's ally and Taiwan's arch rival.

Foreign Minister John Chang, back recently from a failed diplomatic mission to Taipei's departing ally South Africa, greeted Mara at the airport and would host a banquet for the Fiji president later on Thursday, a ministry official said.
Mara, who is scheduled to leave on December 17, plans to meet with Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Friday.
Chang had said in October that Taiwan would push for full diplomatic relations with Fiji, a former British territory in the South Pacific.

The state visit came two months after Fiji and Taiwan signed a mutual-recognition pact, drawing a warning from China not to fall for ploys by Taipei to break free of its Beijing-imposed diplomatic isolation.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, and refuses to recognise any country having official relations with the island.

Beijing scored a big victory in its quest to isolate Taiwan when South Africa said in November it would switch recognition to Beijing from Taipei by the end of 1997. Chang's subsequent visit to Pretoria failed to salvage ties.

The Pretoria fallout would reduce the number of countries that have official relations with Taiwan to 29 -- mostly impoverished states in Africa and central America. Taipei maintains mutual recognition pacts with three Pacific islands that recognise Beijing -- Fiji, Vanuatu and Papua New Guinea.
The Foreign Ministry official said Mara's visit had been arranged long ago and was not related to South Africa's change of recognition.
